questions.stem:
Statements: S = V = Q = X < R.
Conclusions: I. Q < X   II. V < X.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
savings credit access = ze vo mi
savings growth secure = mi lu ni
credit growth rural = re ze ni
access secure rural = re vo lu
savings credit rural = mi re ze
What is the code for “secure”?
questions.explanation: Answer: lu. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: savings = mi, credit = ze, access = vo, growth = ni, secure = lu, rural = re.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 32 km east, turns left and walks 20 km, then turns left and walks 17 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 25. Net displacement is 15 km east and 20 km north. By Pythagoras, √(15² + 20²) = 25 km.

questions.stem: C is the mother of H. E is the son of H. B is the father of H. How is E related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. B is a parent of H, and E is H’s son. Hence E is B’s grandchild.

questions.stem: A is the brother of B. B is the mother of F. G is the father of A and B. How is A related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. A is the brother of F’s mother B. Therefore A is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: F is the only daughter of E. E is the father of F. A is the son of F. C is the sister of E. How is E related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. E is the father of F, and F is A’s mother. Thus E is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 49 candidates, a candidate is 9th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 38. New front rank = 9+3 = 12. Back rank = 49 − 12 + 1 = 38.

questions.stem: In a queue of 57 candidates, a candidate is 21th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 33. New front rank = 21+4 = 25. Back rank = 57 − 25 + 1 = 33.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1400. It is marked above cost and sold at a 10% discount on marked price, earning 25% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 1944.44. Selling price = 1400 × 125/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.9 = 1944.44.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 30 days and B in 45 days. They work together for 2 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 26.67. Use 90 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 90 − 2×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A boat travels 153 km downstream and the same distance upstream. Its still-water speed is 13 km/h and stream speed is 4 km/h. Find the total time (hours).
A invests ₹24000 for 12 months. B invests ₹48000 for 6 months. Total profit is ₹62400. Find B’s share (₹).

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹23000 at 15% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)

questions.stem: A vessel contains 40 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 8. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 8.

questions.stem: The average of 31 numbers is 46. One number, 58, is replaced and the average rises by 6. What is the new number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 244. Total increases by 31 × 6. New number = 58 + 186.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 6 years, their combined age will be 84 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 54. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 12 = 84; x = 18, so father = 54.
